written_before: any external_8b score of any combination rule was computed
question: Plain OR over the existing MoE detectors covers 93.1% of external risks but with unacceptable false alarms; plain AND keeps only the intersection and mechanically pushes the alarm to the later of the two component alarms. Is there an explicit, train-free combination rule that recovers substantially more of the union coverage at a false alarm rate comparable to the current single/AND operating points?

detector_pool.representation_and_direction: taken verbatim from the frame survey's development selection; no new representation search
detector_pool.global_is_the_headline: only the global mode proves the combined signal is MoE-side rather than task-side

rule_family.name: windowed cross-frame quorum
rule_family.definition: with v_d the first alarm chunk of pool member d (-1 = never), the combined alarm is the first chunk q such that at least k members satisfy 0 <= q - v_d <= W and those members span at least f distinct reference frames
rule_family.causal: every vote used at chunk q has v_d <= q
rule_family.s_semantics: at a shared level s every pool member is thresholded at the same quantile of the same unlabeled reference peak distribution, so a k-of-n vote counts how many independent routing views place the episode in the same (1-s) tail

pool_semantics.dedup11: state_action_alignment dropped, because at the selected operating point it and conditional_energy produce near-identical alarm vectors and would double-count one view

special_cases.f=2: corroboration must come from a different reference frame

rule_family.why_this_family: plain AND alarms at max(v_a, v_b), which is unbounded and lands in the high-prior regime. A finite W bounds the confirmation delay to at most W chunks after the first of the k votes, so the rule requires corroboration without surrendering earliness.

baselines_scored_in_the_same_harness: every single pool member at every sensitivity level
every within-mode pairwise AND at the selected level (alarm = max of the two)
plain OR over the pool at every level (= k=1)

selection.external_use: external_8b is scored once, on the shortlist named by this document plus the baselines, after development selection is frozen

objectives_both_predeclared.O1_early: maximise development low_prior_tp (true positives whose matched survival prior is below 0.25)

selection.constraint_provenance: 0.6 low-prior precision and 0.005 timely FPR are the frame survey's own bars; the tighter caps are added because the operating points to beat sit at development timely FPR 0.0007-0.0021
tie_breaks_in_order: smaller k, then smaller W, then smaller f, then smaller level index, then pool name
selection.shortlist_size: one development winner per (mode, pool, objective, cap) = 2 x 2 x 2 x 5 = 40 rules, deduplicated

scoring.survival_prior: per-suite P(risk | still running at chunk q), computed on the cohort being scored, exactly as moe-hb-front-back-0905/experiments/select_early_lock.py does
scoring.lift: precision / mean matched prior at the alarm chunk
scoring.union_coverage_share: tp of the rule divided by tp of plain OR over the same pool at the same level

hard_rules_respected.train_free: no fitted weights, no learned model; every parameter is chosen from the finite grid above by a development ranking
hard_rules_respected.moe_only: every pool member reads hb_router_probs derived quantities only; episode length, outcome and wall-clock never enter a score
hard_rules_respected.causal: a combined alarm at chunk q depends only on component alarms at chunks <= q
hard_rules_respected.survival_baseline: every rule is reported against the matched survival prior, so a rule that raises precision only by firing later shows no lift gain
